title: Then he followed a third way.
subtitle: West, east, and now between the mountains

row.title: a new test
sub: a new chance to do good

then: For the third time the verse says: then he followed a way. Ibn Kathir says he traveled from the east until he reached {idea}a place between two mountains with a valley in between{/idea}, from which Yajuj and Majuj would come to {trap}spread mischief, destroying crops and people{/trap}.
now: Every new phase of life, a new city, a new job, a new child, is another road. {idea}Each one carries its own test and its own chance to do good.{/idea}
old: Once I settle, the tests will stop.
new: Every new road brings a new test, and a new chance to serve.
try: In the newest situation you are in, name one way you can be useful to the people there.

title: A people he could barely understand, still worth helping.
subtitle: Language is no barrier to justice
then: Ibn Kathir says he found a people whose speech he could not understand, {idea}because they were so isolated from other people{/idea}. Even so, they made their need known and {reward}he listened{/reward}.
now: The new family on your street whose language you do not speak. The elderly patient at the clinic who cannot fill in the form. {idea}A barrier of language is not a barrier to kindness.{/idea}
old: If we cannot communicate, I cannot really help.
new: I can still listen and help across a language gap.
try: Help one person today who struggles to communicate, with patience, a smile, or a translation app.

title: They offered to pay him for a barrier.
subtitle: A people asking for protection
then: They told him Yajuj and Majuj were {trap}doing great mischief in the land{/trap}. Ibn Abbas said they wanted to {reward}collect money among themselves to give to him{/reward} so he would build a barrier.
now: Someone asks you for help and quickly offers to pay, almost embarrassed to ask. {idea}How you respond tells them what kind of person you are.{/idea}
old: People in need should pay for the help they get.
new: When I have the power to help, the help itself is the good deed.
try: Help someone today who would have offered to pay, and refuse the payment kindly.

title: What my Lord gave me is better. Just lend me your hands.
subtitle: Turning down the money, asking for effort
then: He answered {reward}with kindness, righteousness and good intentions{/reward}: the power Allah has given me is better than what you collected. Like Sulayman, who said what Allah gave me is better. But he asked them to {idea}help with your labor and equipment{/idea}.
now: A friend in trouble wants you to fix everything and offers a gift. {idea}Refuse the gift, then invite them to work beside you.{/idea} People are lifted by building, not by being carried.
old: Helping someone means doing it all for them.
new: The best help asks nothing in return and invites people to build with me.
try: Next time you help someone today, invite them to do one part with you.

title: Iron blocks, fire, and molten copper poured on top.
subtitle: Building the barrier step by step
then: Ibn Kathir explains he stacked iron blocks {idea}starting at the bottom, until he reached the tops of the mountains{/idea}. Then he lit a fire until it was burning hot. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said the poured metal was {reward}copper{/reward}, some adding molten.
now: Your plan to protect your family from bad habits: limits on screens, time to pray together, honest talks. {idea}One block at a time, heated and sealed. Protection is built, not wished for.{/idea}
old: If I trust Allah, I do not need to plan carefully.
new: Trust in Allah goes with skill, method, and hard work.
try: Write down three concrete steps to protect one thing you care about, and do the first today.

title: They could not climb it, and could not dig through.
subtitle: A barrier that held
then: Ibn Kathir notes the verb for digging is stronger than for climbing, {idea}reflecting the difficulty of the action{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ once woke saying a hole had opened in the barrier, and when asked if they would be destroyed with righteous people among them, he said: {trap}yes, if evil increases{/trap}.
now: You build good walls around your home: a routine, good company, prayer on time. {idea}Walls hold, but the Prophet ﷺ warned what happens when evil increases inside.{/idea}
old: Once I am protected, I can stop paying attention.
new: Protection holds while I keep the good growing and the evil small.
try: Remove one small source of bad influence from your home or phone today.

title: This is a mercy from my Lord, not my achievement.
subtitle: A builder who gave the credit away
then: After building it, he said: {reward}this is a mercy from my Lord{/reward} for the people. Yet he knew it would not last forever: when the promise comes, it will be flattened to the ground, and {idea}the promise of my Lord is ever true{/idea}.
now: You finish the project, the house, the degree. People congratulate you. {idea}Compare the man of the two gardens with this king.{/idea} One said I, the other said my Lord.
old: What I built is my achievement, and it will last.
new: What I built is a mercy from Allah, and it will last only as long as He wills.
try: When someone praises your work today, answer with: Alhamdulillah, it is from Allah.

title: People surging like waves, then the Horn is blown.
subtitle: The barrier falls, the gathering begins
then: Ibn Kathir says this will happen before the Day of Resurrection and after the Dajjal. The Prophet ﷺ said the angel of the Horn already has it in his mouth, waiting for the command. When asked what to say, he taught: {reward}Allah is sufficient for us, and the best Disposer of affairs{/reward}.
now: The news feels like it is surging over you. Wars, prices, illness, headlines one after another. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ gave his companions words for this exact feeling.{/idea}
old: When the world feels like it is falling apart, I have nowhere to stand.
new: Allah is enough for me, and He is the best One to trust with all of it.
try: Say Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil the next time the news makes you anxious today.

title: That Day, Hell is shown openly to those who rejected.
subtitle: What was ignored becomes visible
then: Allah tells us He will {trap}bring it forth for them to see before they enter it{/trap}, which will intensify their distress. The Prophet ﷺ described Hell being brought forth by angels. What was warned about in words becomes {trap}plain to view{/trap}.
now: You read the warnings in the Quran and scroll past them to the comforting verses. {idea}The warnings are shown to you now in words, so you never have to see them any other way.{/idea}
old: I would rather not think about the Fire at all.
new: Allah shows me the warning now so I can stay far from it.
try: Ask Allah tonight: O Allah, protect me from the Fire, three times, with presence.

title: Their eyes were covered from My reminder.
subtitle: Turning a blind eye and a deaf ear
then: Ibn Kathir explains they {trap}neglected it, turning a blind eye and a deaf ear{/trap}, refusing guidance. He cites the verse that whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Gracious is given a devil as a companion. {idea}The covering began with their own looking away.{/idea}
now: You keep the Quran app on the last screen of your phone, behind the games. Every time the reminder pops up, you swipe it away. {idea}Small swipes become a covering over the eyes.{/idea}
old: I am not rejecting anything. I am just busy.
new: Looking away again and again can harden into not seeing at all.
try: Move your Quran app to your home screen today and open it once.
